name: TX-08
label: Likely R

key_factors: R+13 partisan lean makes this a deeply Republican open seat
Steinmann holds a roughly 90-to-1 fundraising edge plus $1.7 million in outside support
Prediction markets price Democratic win odds near 4 percent
Open seat after Morgan Luttrell's retirement is the main source of uncertainty
model.rationale: A 13-point Republican district, an overwhelming Republican money advantage, and market odds near 4 percent for Democrats leave almost no realistic path for an upset despite the incumbent retiring, pointing to a comfortable Republican hold in the mid-teens.
model.watch: Any late surge of Democratic fundraising or outside spending, or fresh polling showing the district far tighter than its lean, would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Morgan Luttrell (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Texas's 8th District, an exurban seat north of Houston, leans Republican by 13 points, and Morgan Luttrell's retirement turns it into an open contest. Republican Jessica Hart Steinmann enters as a heavy favorite, having raised more than $2 million and drawn roughly $1.7 million in outside support. Democrat Laura Jones has raised about $22,000 with no measurable outside spending, leaving her badly outmatched financially.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on the district's fundamentals. Prediction markets give Democrats roughly a 4 percent chance, and the combination of a deep-red electorate and a lopsided money race leaves little realistic path for an upset. The open-seat dynamic is the main uncertainty, but even a strong national Democratic environment would need to overcome a double-digit partisan lean.
